title: Protocol to expand and CRISPR-Cas9 genomic edit murine MAIT cells for subsequent in vivo studies
protocol: Sacrifice the mice following authorized euthanasia methods.
Collect the thymus and store it in a collection plate containing CO2 independent media on ice.
Place the thymus on a 40 μm nylon-filter lying above a 50 mL falcon.
Mechanically dissociate the thymus on top of the filter while thoroughly rinsing with FACS/dissociation buffer.
Centrifuge the 50 mL falcon containing the dissociated thymi at room temperature, 367 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet into a volume of about 200 μL, adding FACS/dissociation buffer if necessary.
Add 6FP:MR1 tetramer to the cell suspension at a final dilution of 1/1000.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Without washing, add MR1:5-OP-RU tetramer labeled with PE at a titrated concentration (usually around 1/800) to the cells.
Centrifuge the tetramer solution containing 10% Fc Block in FACS/dissociation buffer at 4°C and 20,000 g for 10 minutes.
Add the supernatant from the centrifuged tetramer solution to the cell suspension.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Transfer the sample to a 15 mL tube.
Wash with 14 mL of FACS/dissociation buffer and then centrifuge at 4°C and 367 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet into about 200 μL of remaining volume, adding FACS/dissociation buffer if necessary.
Add 150 μL of anti-PE MicroBeads to the 600 μL of cell suspension for magnetic labeling.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 20 minutes.
Wash with 14 mL of FACS/dissociation buffer.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 367 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 3 mL FACS/dissociation buffer.
Place a LS column (1 column for 3 pooled thymi) onto the magnet.
Prime the column by passing 3 mL of FACS/dissociation buffer through it.
Add the 3 mL solution containing the stained thymocytes on the column.
Keep the negative fraction to ensure recovery of cells of interest in case enrichment fails.
Rinse the 15 mL falcon with 3 mL of FACS/dissociation buffer and pass it through the column.
Wash the column with 6 mL of FACS/dissociation buffer.
Remove the column from magnet, place it onto a 15 mL tube.
Add 5 mL of FACS/dissociation buffer to push the cells out of the column using the plunger.
Centrifuge the cells at 4°C, 367 g for 5 minutes.
Proceed to the expansion step.
Keep some of the enriched cells to check for enrichment yield by flow-cytometry.
Count the cells.
Plate 2 million cells in 2 mL of complete culture media solution in a 24-well plate.
Add recombinant mouse IL-2 to each well to reach a concentration of 5 ng/mL.
Add 5-OP-RU to each well to reach a concentration of 150 nM.
Place the plate in a cell culture incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Every 2 days for 9–10 days, add 5 ng/mL of fresh IL-2 to the culture.
Check proliferation and confluence of the cells.
When cells start forming clusters and are above 100% confluence, split them in half.
Top off with 1 mL of new pre-heated media containing fresh IL-2.
Mix 1 μL tracrRNA with 1 μL crRNA.
Anneal sgRNA in a thermocycler using cycling conditions as specified.
Harvest expanded MAIT cells.
Rinse each well thoroughly with PBS to collect all cells.
Count the cells, requiring 2 x 10^6 cells per well in nucleocuvette strip.
Centrifuge the cells at room temperature for 5 minutes at 367 g.
Keep the supernatant for preparing the culture step.
Discard the supernatant and store the pellet for electroporation after an additional centrifugation step.
Prepare a 48 well plate for the following culture step by adding media to each well.
Add 250 μL of cell culture media, 250 μL of fresh media, and 5 ng/mL of fresh IL-2 per well.
Place the plate in a cell culture incubator at 32°C with 5% CO2.
Mix sgRNA (2 μL) and Cas9 (1 μL).
Incubate the mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge the tube containing the cell pellet at 367 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove as much supernatant as possible using a pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 μL of supplemented nucleosolution P3.
For knock-out sample, add 3 μL of the complex sgRNA/Cas9.
For mock sample, add 2 μL of sgRNA and 1 μL of PBS.
Transfer ≃ 25 μL of cells into each well of a nucleocuvette strip.
Start the “DN110” nucleofection program.
Add 100 μL of pre-warmed cell culture media to the nucleocuvette strip.
Incubate the nucleocuvette strip in an incubator at 32°C and 5% CO2 for 10 minutes.
Transfer cells into a 48 well plate previously prepared.
Incubate the 48 well plate in a cell culture incubator at 32°C and 5% CO2 between 24 hours and 3 days.
After 3 days, transfer the plate to an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Evaluate knock-out efficiency through phenotype evaluation if applicable.
Prepare tetramer mix in FACS/dissociation buffer by adding titrated MR1:5-OP-RU tetramer (PE), titrated anti-TCRβ, and 10% Fc block (2.4G2 antibody).
Centrifuge tetramer mix to remove tetramer aggregates at 4°C for 10 minutes at 20,000 g.
Centrifuge 50 μl of cells at room temperature for 5 minutes at 367 g, discard supernatant, and resuspend in tetramer mix.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature with the resuspended cells.
Wash twice: add FACS/dissociation buffer to the mixture, centrifuge at 4°C for 5 minutes at 367 g, discard supernatant after each wash.
Resuspend pellet in extracellular mix containing titrated antibodies and 10% Fc Block in FACS/dissociation buffer.
Incubate for 20 min at 4°C with the resuspended mixture.
Wash twice: add FACS/dissociation buffer, centrifuge at 4°C for 5 minutes at 367 g, discard supernatant after each wash.
Resuspend in FACS/dissociation buffer and proceed to flow-cytometry acquisition.
Inject anesthetic and analgesic in mice according to local regulations.
Shave upper-back hair of mice.
Apply hair removal cream for 2 minutes.
Clean and disinfect epilated skin.
Perform full-thickness wound using a 4 mm diameter biopsy punch on one side slightly off the midline of the mouse’s back.
Apply adhesive on one side of a silicone ring.
Center silicone ring over the wound and suture using 6-0 nylon thread: 4 stitches for short term needs (<5 days), 6 stitches for long term needs (up to 14 days).
Cover the wound: Add 1.4 cm piece of non-woven compresses.
Overlay with transparent occlusive dressing (e.g., 3M).
Wrap mouse with cohesive contention strip (e.g., 3M coheban) of about 2 cm wide and with a length of about 1.2 times the mouse circumference.
Regularly check wound every 2/3 days to assess suture status and change dressing to avoid infection.
Inject the modified expanded MAIT cells one day following the excision.
Collect the knock-out and wild-type cells in two separate tubes.
Thoroughly rinse all wells with PBS.
Stain a fraction of the cells to assess: MAIT cell purity, phenotype and numbers.
Based on cell count obtained by flow-cytometry, prepare a mix of CXCR6-KO and WT MAIT cells at a 1:1 ratio in 100 μL of sterile PBS and inject intravenously.
Keep a part of the injected mixture for flow cytometry analysis.
Sacrifice the mice following authorized euthanasia method.
Collect full-thickness skin samples in a collection plate containing CO2 independent media on ice.
Incise a 1 cm² area of skin encompassing the wound and surrounding rims for sample collection.
Incise a 1 cm² area of contralateral control skin from the opposite side off the mouse’s midline for comparison.
Prepare a single-cell suspension from the collected skin samples.
Place samples at 37°C in a 24 well-plate with 1 mL of 500 CU Dispase for 45 minutes.
Transfer and chop skin sample in a new well containing 1.5 mL of skin digestion buffer.
Incubate the chopped skin sample 1 hour and 45 minutes at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Transfer and scratch digested skin samples on ice using the back end of a syringe plunger on a 40 μm nylon-filter placed on top of a 50 mL tube.
Thoroughly wash filter and plunger using FACS/dissociation buffer.
Centrifuge cells at 4°C, 367 g for 5 minutes and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 3.1 mL cold 1× PBS and transfer into a 15 mL tube.
Add 900 μL of debris removal solution and gently pipette up and down (5–10 times) to homogenize.
Gently overlay with 4 mL cold 1× PBS.
Centrifuge cells at 4°C, 3000 g for 10 minutes.
Aspirate top two phases carefully without disturbing the visible "white" cloud above the pellet.
Fill tube with 15 mL cold 1× PBS.
Gently invert the tube 3 times.
Centrifuge cells at 4°C, 1000 g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Proceed to cell staining following the phenotype evaluation section.
